kaigo-housework-01-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Distinguish IADL from eating actions and explain the full cooking sequence.
Respect the person’s chosen participation scope and check assistance needs and wishes to stop.

kaigo-housework-01-knowledge-0.heading: Housework and IADL
paragraphs: Housework includes cooking, cleaning, laundry, clothing organization and shopping, which support everyday life. It is part of instrumental activities of daily living (IADL). Eating independently differs from preparing ingredients and tools and cooking. Ask about habits and wishes, separating desired participation from assistance needs.

kaigo-housework-01-knowledge-1.heading: Cooking sequence and checks
paragraphs: Cooking is more than heating food. It includes planning menus, obtaining ingredients, preparing and plating food, serving and cleaning up. Check condition, allergies and dietary plans to choose suitable ingredients and methods. Liking a dish does not establish absence of allergy. Avoid spreading contamination from raw ingredients to cooked food or clean tools.

kaigo-housework-01-knowledge-2.heading: Food culture and partial participation
paragraphs: Familiar tastes and seasonal or celebration dishes can bring enjoyment. However, do not assume preferences from nationality or age; ask the person. Participating in one part, such as choosing ingredients or explaining presentation wishes, also matters. Completing every housework task is not a condition of independence.

kaigo-housework-01-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Onodera-san is seated stably at an activity table and wants to do a little familiar housework. A basket of clean towels is within reach according to the plan. Discuss which task to join. This is not practice in carrying, hanging laundry or posture changes. In this situation, hanging is assigned to staff.

kaigo-housework-01-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Onodera-san is seated stably at an activity table and wants to do a little familiar housework. A basket of clean towels is within reach according to the plan. Discuss which task to join. This is not practice in carrying, hanging laundry or posture changes. In this situation, hanging is assigned to staff.
Fumi Onodera: I’d like to do a little housework, but I’m not planning to put away all the laundry today.
Care worker: Let’s choose what you want to do now rather than everything. Which part would you like to try?
Fumi Onodera: I’d like to fold two small towels. I’d like staff to hang the laundry.
Care worker: You’ve chosen to fold two small towels. Staff will do the hanging.
Fumi Onodera: Even with two, can I leave some if I want to stop partway?
Care worker: Please tell us if you want to stop. We’ll discuss the remaining work with the responsible staff member.
Fumi Onodera: Then I’ll try one at a time. I’ll tell you how many I finish.
Care worker: One at a time. We’ll check finished and remaining work separately and won’t add tasks you haven’t chosen.

kaigo-housework-01-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Housework participation check
Onodera-san chose to fold two small towels. Staff will hang the laundry. Check any wish to stop partway. The activity has not started, so no towels are folded yet.

kaigo-language-transfer-239.heading: Finished and remaining work
paragraphs: Person: I’m getting tired, so please let staff do the rest. I’ve folded two so far. Staff member: Two are done, and the rest remain.

The person reports folding two and asks staff to do the rest. They do not say the entire basket is finished. Distinguish their words from actually verified results and check responsibility for the remaining work.

kaigo-housework-02-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Check consent to organizing and disposal and the desired locations with the person.
Check safety, usability and privacy as well as cleanliness.

kaigo-housework-02-knowledge-0.heading: Check before organizing
paragraphs: Cleaning removes trash, dust and dirt to support safe, comfortable living. An old-looking item may matter to the person. Separately ask what to sort, where to put it and what may be discarded. Avoid appearance-driven changes that prevent the person finding belongings.

kaigo-housework-02-knowledge-1.heading: Living surroundings suited to the person and activity
paragraphs: Consider temperature, humidity, ventilation, light, routes, grab bars, item locations and privacy together. The goal is safe activity and reassurance suited to physical and mental condition. An uncluttered floor is not enough if grab bars cannot be used or needed items cannot be reached.

kaigo-housework-02-knowledge-2.heading: Equipment and checks after work
paragraphs: Moving furniture and using machines or chemicals require facility procedures and product instructions. Do not independently mix cleaners or choose concentrations. Cleaning away dirt differs from disinfection by a specified method. Afterward, check locations with the person and whether needed items can actually be used.

kaigo-housework-02-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Hasebe-san wants to organize sheets and blankets received from storage. Sort by name labels rather than age, and discuss locations. Do not carry heavy items, read private papers or discard belongings in this exercise.

kaigo-housework-02-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Hasebe-san wants to organize sheets and blankets received from storage. Sort by name labels rather than age, and discuss locations. Do not carry heavy items, read private papers or discard belongings in this exercise.
Kenichi Hasebe: I want to put away sheets and blankets. Please sort by name labels rather than new or old.
Care worker: By name labels, not newness. Could you also tell me where you want the sorted items?
Kenichi Hasebe: Things with my name go on the left shelf. For ones with only the facility name, ask storage whether they can be returned.
Care worker: Your named items go on the left shelf. I won’t return facility-name-only items yet; I’ll check with storage first.
Kenichi Hasebe: This blanket has no label. Don’t put it in the discard pile.
Care worker: I’ll leave the unlabeled blanket where it is rather than putting it in either group. Let’s discuss its place after ownership is established.
Kenichi Hasebe: That’s fine. Don’t touch the top shelf of the curtained shelving unit.
Care worker: I won’t touch the top shelf. We’ll work only with the agreed items and check the sorting together afterward.

kaigo-housework-02-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Agreement before organizing
Sort by name labels. Hasebe-san’s named items go on the left shelf. Check with storage whether facility-name-only items may be returned. Leave the unlabeled blanket as it is. Top shelf excluded. No disposal agreed.

kaigo-language-transfer-236.heading: Timing conditions
paragraphs: Person: Please open the window after I finish changing clothes. Staff member: After changing, understood.
The requested time to open the window is after changing is complete. This is not consent to open it now. Check privacy and wishes.

kaigo-housework-03-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Check the update date and changes and communicate unchanged dates and times too.
Connect eligible people, deadlines, locations and actions, distinguishing materials requests from attendance.

kaigo-housework-03-knowledge-0.heading: Read a notice’s target and conditions
paragraphs: For notices, check who they address, when, where, what happens and conditions. Do not extend a ban in one place to the entire facility or turn a materials-request deadline into an attendance deadline. Distinguish issue or update dates from effective dates.

kaigo-housework-03-knowledge-1.heading: Compare old and updated documents
paragraphs: If notices differ, establish which is currently valid. Read unchanged dates, times and conditions as well as updates. For event plans, check participants, numbers, location and assigned tasks. Similar professional titles do not justify swapping responsibilities.

kaigo-housework-03-knowledge-2.heading: Check unknown information
paragraphs: Explain in short parts and check wishes and understanding. Do not invent missing conditions; ask the person responsible. Rules in practice notices belong to that fictional facility. Do not memorize them as universal; check current workplace guidance and procedures.

kaigo-housework-03-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Kawase-san asks you to compare two notices about a book-introduction event. Only the venue changed in the update. Requesting materials differs from attending. Do not treat this fictional schedule as an actual facility schedule.

kaigo-housework-03-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Kawase-san asks you to compare two notices about a book-introduction event. Only the venue changed in the update. Requesting materials differs from attending. Do not treat this fictional schedule as an actual facility schedule.
Naoto Kawase: Please check the book-event notices. There are two; which will you use?
Care worker: The one updated October 12 saying it replaces the old notice. I’ll also check the changes.
Naoto Kawase: The old notice says October 16 at 2:00 p.m. in Lounge 1. What changed in the update?
Care worker: The venue changed to Lounge 2. October 16 at 2:00 p.m. is unchanged.
Naoto Kawase: It says, ‘Request materials by the 15th if wanted.’ Does everyone attending need to apply?
Care worker: The 15th deadline applies to people wanting materials. The notice says attendance itself needs no application.
Naoto Kawase: Then tell people who did not request materials about the venue change too.
Care worker: I’ll tell people wishing to attend about the change to Lounge 2. I’ll check materials requests and attendance wishes separately.

kaigo-housework-03-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Book-introduction event / Updated October 12
This notice replaces the old one. Starts October 16 at 2:00 p.m. Only the venue changes, from Lounge 1 to Lounge 2. No application needed for attendance. Request materials at reception by October 15 if wanted.

kaigo-language-transfer-258.heading: Conditions for each location
paragraphs: Eating and drinking are prohibited in the resource room. In the break room, drinks are allowed at designated seats.
The ban applies to the resource room. In the break room, drinks are allowed only at designated seats, not anywhere. Do not generalize this fictional notice’s conditions to other facilities.

kaigo-housework-04-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Explain handling suited to fabric and dirt and the distinction between clean and dirty items.
Record machine completion, actual checks, personal wishes and handover separately.

kaigo-housework-04-knowledge-0.heading: Check fabric, labels and dirt
paragraphs: Laundry keeps clothing and bedding clean and supports healthy living. Methods must match materials and care labels. For waste, blood or vomit contamination, check facility handling appropriate to the risk and separate from clean items. Do not shake dirty fabric vigorously or use identical chemicals, temperatures and machine settings for all materials.

kaigo-housework-04-knowledge-1.heading: Distinguish stages from states
paragraphs: Washing, hanging or drying, checking dryness, folding and returning items each require checks. ‘Become dry’ is a change of state; ‘dry something’ is an action to produce that state. Machine completion does not prove every item dry. Do not extend one item’s result to the entire basket.

kaigo-housework-04-knowledge-2.heading: Maintain cleanliness and return to the right person
paragraphs: Dirty storage or transport containers may contaminate laundry again. Check cleanliness, dryness, damage and ownership before folding and storing in a clean place. Ask about habits and participation wishes. One damp towel edge does not establish all items are wet or the machine broken.

kaigo-housework-04-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You prepare a laundry-check note with Kishimoto-san. The machine showed completion at 10:20. At 10:25, as an assigned task, you touched one towel’s edge and found dampness. Other towels are unconfirmed. Onodera-san wants that towel in the afternoon. Do not operate machines or decide drying methods in this practice.

kaigo-housework-04-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You prepare a laundry-check note with Kishimoto-san. The machine showed completion at 10:20. At 10:25, as an assigned task, you touched one towel’s edge and found dampness. Other towels are unconfirmed. Onodera-san wants that towel in the afternoon. Do not operate machines or decide drying methods in this practice.
Misaki Kishimoto: I’m thinking of writing ‘all dry.’ The machine showed completion at 10:20, correct?
Care worker: The display was checked, but that alone doesn’t establish everything is dry. I checked only the edge of one towel.
Misaki Kishimoto: When did you check it, and what was it like?
Care worker: I touched it at 10:25, and that edge was damp. I haven’t checked other towels yet.
Misaki Kishimoto: Onodera-san said they want that towel in the afternoon. How will you record it?
Care worker: As Onodera-san’s stated wish to use it in the afternoon, separate from checking dryness or completing handover.
Misaki Kishimoto: Understood. Let’s consult the responsible worker about unchecked items.
Care worker: I’ll report display time, checking time and condition, and the person’s wishes separately. Other items remain unconfirmed.

kaigo-housework-04-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
October 18 / Laundry check
10:20: Machine completion display checked.10:25: Touched one towel edge; dampness present. Other towels unconfirmed. Onodera-san says, ‘I’d like that towel this afternoon.’ Handover not performed.

kaigo-language-transfer-243.heading: Wiping scope and results
paragraphs: Person: I wiped the right half of the desk. The left is not done yet. Staff member: The right is finished; the left remains.
The person reports wiping the right half, not the left. Do not record the whole desk as wiped. Judging it clean also requires checking the result.

kaigo-housework-05-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Prioritize urgent contact over recording and separate observations from assumed causes.
Report confirmed responses, observation scope and unconfirmed matters.

kaigo-housework-05-knowledge-0.heading: Responding to accidents and near misses
paragraphs: After an accident, prioritize personal safety, needed help and contact through facility procedures. Do not complete records or determine causes before contacting help. Near misses also reveal hazards and support prevention. Do not independently conclude whether injury exists or repair and reuse equipment.

kaigo-housework-05-knowledge-1.heading: Separate observations from guesses
paragraphs: Report who saw and did what, when and where, and the result. Include unknown causes or effects. Seeing nobody on arrival does not establish nobody was there earlier. A fallen or broken item does not establish someone’s carelessness.

kaigo-housework-05-knowledge-2.heading: Share information to prevent recurrence
paragraphs: After reporting, the team reviews surroundings, equipment, pre-task checks and coordination. Blame alone does not prevent recurrence. In fire or disaster, follow trained roles and emergency-contact methods; report writing must not delay calls or safety measures.

kaigo-housework-05-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 11:08, you found a cart caught on the linen-store doorway and immediately contacted the responsible worker. They stopped its use and prevented entry to that area. You now give Kawase-san an additional private report. This does not teach repair or delay initial contact for records.

kaigo-housework-05-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 11:08, you found a cart caught on the linen-store doorway and immediately contacted the responsible worker. They stopped its use and prevented entry to that area. You now give Kawase-san an additional private report. This does not teach repair or delay initial contact for records.
Naoto Kawase: I received the earlier contact. Please give an additional report now safety is secured. When and where did this happen?
Care worker: At 11:08, at the linen-store entrance, I saw a cart loaded with linens caught on the door. I contacted the responsible worker then.
Naoto Kawase: Tell me the worker’s response within what you confirmed.
Care worker: I confirmed they stopped the cart’s use and kept others from entering the area. It has not been used again.
Naoto Kawase: What do you know about the cause and people receiving care at the scene?
Care worker: The cause is unconfirmed. No person receiving care was visible in that area while I watched, but I haven’t checked earlier circumstances.
Naoto Kawase: I’ll check earlier circumstances and effects. Record only what you confirmed.
Care worker: I’ll record finding and contact times, location and confirmed action. Cause, earlier circumstances and effects remain unconfirmed.

kaigo-housework-05-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Additional report / October 19
11:08: Found cart caught on linen-store doorway. Contacted responsible worker at the same time. Confirmed stopped use and action to prevent area entry. No resumed use. Cause, prior circumstances and effects unconfirmed.

kaigo-language-transfer-254.heading: Order in a training schedule
paragraphs: Training schedule: First check the contact person, then inspect the exit, and finally check the assembly point.
The second item is inspecting the exit. The order is contact person, exit and assembly point. This practice schedule is not a response sequence applying to every actual fire.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Practice record: At 2:12 p.m., noticed Morikawa-san’s sudden breathlessness in the first-floor lounge. The person also reported difficulty breathing. Immediately called for help. Kishimoto confirmed connection to 119 and is responding with assisting staff under instructions. Nurse Fujino arrived. Cause, earlier condition and recovery status are unconfirmed.
Separate item case: From 3:20 to 3:23 p.m., observed the area visible from the book-storage entrance. Saw a book fall from a shelf during that time. After reporting, confirmed the responsible worker stopped shelf use. Cause and circumstances before observation are unknown.

kaigo-housework-06-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Distinguish the purposes of reporting, communication and consultation.
Check sending, receipt, acceptance of responsibility and completion separately.

kaigo-housework-06-knowledge-0.heading: Reporting, communication, consultation and handoffs
paragraphs: Reporting communicates action results or condition changes. Communication connects information so relevant people can work together. Consultation seeks opinions or help with difficulties or decisions. Handoffs share conditions, responses and remaining tasks so the next worker can continue support.

kaigo-housework-06-knowledge-1.heading: Check whether information was received
paragraphs: Recipients listen to important information, record as needed and repeat who needs what done and by when. Making a call, connecting, accepting responsibility and finishing are four different states. An unanswered call or a name on a roster does not confirm acceptance.

kaigo-housework-06-knowledge-2.heading: Hand over exceptions and unfinished matters
paragraphs: A general handoff schedule may have exceptions for a person or day. Read exceptions before acting and share needed information with the right person, place and method. Do not disclose personal information publicly. If contact fails, follow facility methods for the next response and do not mark complete before results are known.

kaigo-housework-06-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Before shift change, at a staff desk, you prepare to pass Onodera-san’s laundry wish to the next worker. The 3:40 p.m. extension call was unanswered. Kishimoto accepts the next contact and agrees to report by 4:00 p.m. Assigning responsibility does not mean the wish reached the recipient.

kaigo-housework-06-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Before shift change, at a staff desk, you prepare to pass Onodera-san’s laundry wish to the next worker. The 3:40 p.m. extension call was unanswered. Kishimoto accepts the next contact and agrees to report by 4:00 p.m. Assigning responsibility does not mean the wish reached the recipient.
Misaki Kishimoto: This concerns passing Onodera-san’s laundry wish to the next worker. The note says an extension call was made at 3:40 p.m.
Care worker: That records a call. Is connection, delivery of the wish and receipt also confirmed?
Misaki Kishimoto: No. It was unanswered and has not reached them. I’ll contact the responsible worker now.
Care worker: It has not reached them yet. You’ll take the next contact, Kishimoto-san; by when can you tell me the result?
Misaki Kishimoto: By the 4:00 p.m. shift change. If I cannot connect, I’ll report that too.
Care worker: Confirmed: Kishimoto-san will contact them and report by 4:00 p.m. For now, delivery to the responsible worker stays incomplete.
Misaki Kishimoto: Please do that. After I report the result, let’s also check what was received.
Care worker: On receiving the result, I’ll check who received what and update the record. Accepting the contact task alone does not mean completion.

kaigo-housework-06-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Handoff field / As of 3:50 p.m.
3:40 p.m.: Extension call made; unanswered. The wish has not reached the next worker. Kishimoto accepts the next contact and agrees to report by 4:00 p.m. Contact result and recipient remain unconfirmed.

kaigo-language-transfer-267.heading: Exceptions after ‘however’
paragraphs: Tomorrow, three people return by car at 3:00 p.m. However, Nakamura-san’s family will collect them at 2:00 p.m.
Besides the general schedule, Nakamura-san has an exception: family collection at 2:00 p.m. Do not summarize everyone as leaving by car at 3:00. Connect person, time and who collects them.

kaigo-housework-07-summary.heading: Today’s learning goals
paragraphs: Explain what can be determined from each document type.
Do not replace personal consent with family wishes; hand over unfinished matters.

kaigo-housework-07-knowledge-0.heading: Respect the person’s chosen housework scope
paragraphs: For cooking, cleaning and laundry, identify purposes, stages and barriers to participation. Wanting to fold towels does not mean accepting washing and hanging too. A family disposal request does not replace personal consent. Separate independent actions and assistance needs; staff should not decide everything.

kaigo-housework-07-knowledge-1.heading: Document types and what they establish
paragraphs: When reading tables, connect rows, columns, people, dates and activities. A menu does not replace individual allergy information; a work schedule is not a completed-action record. A consultation-item list does not prove handover. Checking document purpose prevents inventing results not stated.

kaigo-housework-07-knowledge-2.heading: Preserve information sources and corrections
paragraphs: In handoffs, distinguish whose words are reported, directly confirmed facts and unchecked matters. If documents differ, check the basis and scope of changes and preserve correction history through facility methods. Beyond memorizing missed answers, practice identifying people, deadlines, exceptions and completion in other documents.

kaigo-housework-07-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Morikawa-san’s daughter Megumi asks about the facility’s book-consultation notice. Morikawa-san is absent. This morning’s record says they have not chosen books to send. This stage accepts a consultation list, not actual books. Explain the notice and pass the consultation request to the responsible staff member.

kaigo-housework-07-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Morikawa-san’s daughter Megumi asks about the facility’s book-consultation notice. Morikawa-san is absent. This morning’s record says they have not chosen books to send. This stage accepts a consultation list, not actual books. Explain the notice and pass the consultation request to the responsible staff member.
Megumi Morikawa: I’d like to organize my mother’s bookshelf. The notice says ‘book reception.’ May I bring everything?
Care worker: This notice accepts a consultation list, not books themselves at this stage. We also need to check which books your mother wants to consider.
Megumi Morikawa: It says lists are due by the 22nd, with personal consultation afterward. Has my mother already chosen books?
Care worker: This morning’s record says Morikawa-san stated, ‘I haven’t chosen books to send yet.’ We’ll ask about current wishes again.
Megumi Morikawa: Then I won’t bring everything. Could you pass on that I’d like to discuss the list with my mother?
Care worker: I’ll tell the responsible worker that you, Megumi-san, want to discuss the list. I won’t treat it as your mother’s consent to send books.
Megumi Morikawa: Please do. I haven’t decided when to discuss it with her yet.
Care worker: I’ll hand over the consultation request and undecided date separately. I won’t record book selection or handover as complete.

kaigo-housework-07-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Book consultation reception / Updated October 20
Submit a consultation list to the responsible worker by October 22. Do not bring books. Afterward, consult the person to select items.
Today’s handoff: Megumi requested discussing the list with her mother. Consultation date undecided. No completed selection or handover.

kaigo-language-transfer-262.heading: Roles at an event
paragraphs: Reading group: People receiving care choose books. Staff prepare the venue. Families help at reception.
People receiving care choose books, staff prepare the venue and families help at reception. Families are not assigned to choose books instead of the person.

kaigo-gap-services-01-reading.heading: Read records and notices
paragraphs:
Service consultation note: Differences between home visits, day services and residential care explained. Personal wishes, eligibility conditions and start date unconfirmed. No application made.
Belongings consultation notice (practice): Until October 17, accept only consultation forms listing craft materials. From the 18th, consult the person and select items. Do not bring belongings.
Megumi requested making the form with her mother. Consultation date undecided. Her mother has not chosen items, and no handover occurred.

kaigo-depth-39.heading: Connect menus, personal wishes and hygiene
paragraphs: Cooking considers accessible nutrition together with enjoyment and culture. Requests for traditional or seasonal foods do not justify ignoring confirmed allergies or planned food texture. Chopping alone does not necessarily achieve the planned softness.

First identify whose meal it is and check wishes, dietary plan and ingredient labels, then discuss participation. Prepare clean tools and prevent contamination through contact between raw ingredients and cooked food. Follow facility and product methods for cooking and storage rather than independently setting uniform heating times or temperatures. Before serving, verify the person, dish and texture; afterward, clean equipment and work areas.

Supporting participation means neither assigning sharp-tool or heat tasks beyond ability nor taking over everything. Check independent actions and safety conditions. Do not reject food culture based on age alone. Consult dietary-plan staff when decisions such as alternative ingredients are needed.
This explanation teaches purposes and checks. Actual work follows personal condition, dietary plans, equipment and product instructions, and facility training.

kaigo-depth-40.heading: Protect safety and ownership wishes during cleaning
paragraphs: Cleaning supports safe, comfortable living as well as dirt removal. Do not confuse cleaning with completed disinfection by an appropriate method. Items staff regard as unnecessary may matter to the person.

Ask the work scope, what may be moved or discarded and return locations. Prepare tools suitable for surfaces and avoid carrying contamination from dirty to clean areas. Check chemical labels and facility methods; do not mix independently. With wet floors, protect people passing and confirm dryness through facility methods.

Afterward, return belongings and the call device to agreed positions and check usability. Stable item locations can guide people with reduced vision. A clean room does not resolve inability to call, unusable grab bars or unauthorized disposal of photos.
Moving heavy furniture and using machines or chemicals follow facility methods and training. Do not invent formulations or work techniques from this explanation.

kaigo-depth-41.heading: Laundry checks for fabric and clean–dirty separation
paragraphs: Keeping clothing and bedding clean requires fabric-appropriate laundry. Items contaminated with waste, vomit or blood from a person with infection, for example, are separated from ordinary laundry and handled through facility methods. Also separate dirty-item containers and transport routes from clean storage.

Check ownership, care labels and dirt, then prepare necessary protective equipment and containers. Store and transport through facility methods; do not shake fabric vigorously and spread contamination. Use methods suited to fabric and condition without independently increasing temperature or chemicals.

At the transition from dirty to clean work, remove gloves appropriately and perform hand hygiene. After laundry, check cleanliness, dryness, damage and ownership and fold and store in clean places. Do not put clean sheets on an untreated cart that carried dirty items.

Machine completion or fragrance alone does not establish completed dryness or hygiene checks. Do not record ‘disinfected’ based only on ordinary washing. Actual processing follows facility and product methods and training.

kaigo-housework-01-transfer-legacy.heading: A wish to arrange three placemats
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The person wants to arrange three placemats, not prepare the entire dining room.
Check the chosen three-item scope, help needed and how to say they want to stop. Do not add unchosen preparation; discuss remaining work with the person responsible.

kaigo-housework-02-transfer-legacy.heading: Separate magazine sorting from disposal
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The person wants magazines sorted into ‘still reading’ and ‘decide after thinking.’ One magazine’s category remains undecided.
Check their criteria and wait for the undecided magazine. ‘Think about it’ does not mean consent to disposal; check discarding separately.

kaigo-housework-03-transfer-legacy.heading: Changed locations and unchanged conditions
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A different practice notice changes only the book collection point. Only people wanting printed copies have an application deadline.
Check the valid notice and communicate the new collection point and unchanged conditions. Do not extend printed-copy application requirements to every participant.

kaigo-housework-04-transfer-legacy.heading: Two checked items do not establish the whole
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A container device’s completion light is on. Only two items inside have actually been checked. The person wants collection by evening.
Record display, the two checked results and the person’s wish with their information sources separately. Other items remain unconfirmed. Hearing a collection wish is not completed handover.

kaigo-housework-05-transfer-legacy.heading: Additional report of a fallen book
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] After initial contact, you confirmed the responsible worker stopped shelf use. You saw a book fall but do not know the cause.
Report time, place, observation scope, the falling book, confirmed stopped use and unknown cause. Do not repair the shelf before contacting help.

kaigo-housework-06-transfer-legacy.heading: Unanswered booking contact
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A booking message remains unanswered. A colleague accepts a checking call and says they will report by 4:00 p.m.
Record who accepted contact and the reporting deadline. Leave booking and recipient agreement unconfirmed, distinguishing sending from receipt.

kaigo-housework-07-transfer-legacy.heading: Consultation reception and item handover
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] Repair consultations initially accept only item-name lists. The family wants to remove all the person’s belongings.

Explain that actual items are not accepted yet and consult the responsible person about an opportunity to check personal wishes. Hand over the family request separately from unconfirmed personal consent, selection and handover.

kaigo-housework-01-words.heading: Vocabulary and useful expressions for reference
paragraphs: This is a reference for checking needed words, not a requirement to learn every word today. Choose words for today’s situation and return later to check unfamiliar ones.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person wants to do or have done.
観察（かんさつ） — Observation: carefully checking words, appearance and other information to understand conditions or changes.
家事（かじ） — Housework: tasks maintaining daily life, such as cooking, cleaning and laundry.
洗濯物（せんたくもの） — Laundry: items awaiting washing or already washed. Check the processing stage too.
たたむ（たたむ） — Fold: arrange fabric in overlapping layers, distinct from washing or hanging it.
干す（ほす） — Hang to dry: spread or hang laundry or similar items for drying.
片付ける（かたづける） — Put away: organize items into agreed places, not discard them without permission.
毛布（もうふ） — Blanket: thick fabric bedding placed over the body.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-intro.heading: Emergency requests and handoff for sudden breathlessness
paragraphs: [Learning simulation: no actual emergency call] At 2:12 p.m., you notice Morikawa-san’s sudden breathlessness in the first-floor lounge, and they also report difficulty breathing. Help is called immediately. Kishimoto confirms connection to 119 and responds with assisting staff under instructions. Nurse Fujino arrives beside the person. The following conversation practices handoff to Fujino; completing it is not a condition before requesting an ambulance. Cause and recovery remain unconfirmed.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-knowledg.heading: Do not delay emergency requests for sudden breathlessness
paragraphs: Japan’s Fire and Disaster Management Agency lists sudden shortness of breath or difficulty breathing among symptoms for which an ambulance should be called without hesitation. Immediately request on-site help and a 119 call. Do not wait to identify the cause, complete records or have the supervisor arrive. Symptoms outside this example can also require emergency action.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-knowledg.heading: Continue necessary help after calling
paragraphs: Briefly communicate location and known condition and listen to the dispatcher’s questions. Follow any first-aid guidance and coordinate with on-site staff. Calling an ambulance does not complete assistance. This material does not replace first-aid training or teach medication doses or resuscitation techniques.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-knowledg.heading: Separate noticing time from onset time
paragraphs: Do not replace the time a worker noticed a change with an exact disease-onset time. Separate observations, the person’s words and unknowns. State who is doing what only within confirmation. A nurse’s arrival does not establish recovery or safety.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-knowledg.heading: Emergency action first, records afterward
paragraphs: Prioritize help and emergency contact, then record time, location, observations, personal statements and confirmed responses. The later book-storage item report is a separate situation. It does not mean checking shelves or books before helping the breathless person. Do not add assumed causes or unseen conditions.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-case.heading: Do not confuse initial action with handoff
paragraphs: Appropriate response: Request emergency and on-site help when sudden breathlessness is noticed, then briefly hand over observations and ongoing responses to the arriving nurse.
Inappropriate thinking: Wait to call until eight dialogue exchanges finish, or record recovery because the nurse arrived. This confuses conversation-practice sequence with emergency priorities.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-transfer.heading: Report a separate item case with scope limits
paragraphs: [Separate item case after emergency contact] From 3:20 to 3:23 p.m., you observe the area visible from the book-storage entrance and see a book fall from a shelf. Stopped shelf use by the responsible worker is confirmed. Cause, prior circumstances and unseen areas are unknown.
Tell Kawase-san time, place, observation scope, event, confirmed response and unknowns separately. Do not repair it yourself or claim nobody was anywhere in the storage room.

Example wording: From 3:20 to 3:23 p.m., in the area visible from the book-storage entrance, I saw a book fall from a shelf. I confirmed the responsible worker stopped shelf use. Cause and prior circumstances are unknown, and I cannot say what happened outside the visible area.
This is an offline exercise. Do not call 119 for practice. It does not teach waiting for dialogue before an emergency call, giving medication or independently improvising resuscitation.

kaigo-gap-services-01-intro.heading: Separate service forms from personal wishes
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Megumi asks about service types to discuss future options with her mother, Morikawa-san. This is not a decision to leave the current facility, and personal records are not opened. Daytime social interaction is currently Megumi’s wish; her mother’s wishes have not been heard. Staff explain general differences and check appropriate consultation routes.

kaigo-gap-services-01-knowledge-0.heading: Focus on where support is received
paragraphs: Broad forms include staff visiting the home, the person attending a facility during daytime and using a facility as a home. Distinguishing who goes where helps understanding. These three forms neither cover every service nor determine what suits one person.

kaigo-gap-services-01-knowledge-1.heading: Distinguish home visits from day services
paragraphs: With home visits, staff go to the person’s home to support them. With day services, the person travels to a facility, receives support and returns. Daytime attendance alone does not make the facility their home. Check specific service names and details with the consultation contact.

kaigo-gap-services-01-knowledge-2.heading: Residential care differs from daytime interaction
paragraphs: With residential care, the facility becomes the place to live. A family wish for daytime social interaction alone does not establish a need to move home. Some services combine forms; these three categories alone cannot determine eligibility.

kaigo-gap-services-01-knowledge-3.heading: Connect the person with consultation
paragraphs: Families may ask general information, but their wishes do not replace personal choice or consent. Ask how the person wants to live and coordinate with a care manager or appropriate consultation service. Reception staff do not promise availability, eligibility, cost, start dates or completed applications. This situation has only a consultation request, with no date set.

kaigo-gap-services-01-case.heading: Separate explanation, personal consent and application
paragraphs: Appropriate approach: After explaining general forms, consult the responsible person about hearing Morikawa-san’s wishes and referral to a consultation service. Leave eligibility and start date unconfirmed.

Inappropriate approach: Saying a service can start tomorrow and an application is complete because family wants daytime interaction. Explanation, consent, eligibility checks and application each need confirmation.

kaigo-gap-emergency-handover-01-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Learning simulation: no actual emergency call] At 2:12 p.m., you notice Morikawa-san’s sudden breathlessness in the first-floor lounge, and they also report difficulty breathing. Help is called immediately. Kishimoto confirms connection to 119 and responds with assisting staff under instructions. Nurse Fujino arrives beside the person. The following conversation practices handoff to Fujino; completing it is not a condition before requesting an ambulance. Cause and recovery remain unconfirmed.
Aya Fujino: Help and the emergency request are underway. Briefly tell me what is confirmed.
Care worker: At 2:12 p.m. in the first-floor lounge, Morikawa-san suddenly appeared breathless. They also said breathing was difficult.
Aya Fujino: What does that time represent? Do you know the cause?
Care worker: It is when I noticed the change. I don’t know the earlier condition or cause. I haven’t determined a disease.
Aya Fujino: Who has done what regarding the emergency request?
Care worker: I immediately called for help. Kishimoto-san is connected to 119 and responding with assisting staff under instructions.
Aya Fujino: I’ll respond here. How will you handle unknowns in the record?
Care worker: I’ll separate observations, the person’s own words and confirmed responses. I’ll record cause and earlier condition as unknown, not recovery.

kaigo-gap-services-01-dialogue.heading: Practice conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Megumi asks about service types to discuss future options with her mother, Morikawa-san. This is not a decision to leave the current facility, and personal records are not opened. Daytime social interaction is currently Megumi’s wish; her mother’s wishes have not been heard. Staff explain general differences and check appropriate consultation routes.
Megumi Morikawa: I’m thinking about my mother’s future. Does a home visit mean she goes to a facility during the day?
Care worker: A home visit means staff come to your home. It differs from the person traveling to a facility during the day.
Megumi Morikawa: If she uses a facility in daytime, does that mean moving there?
Care worker: Day services mean attending during the day and returning. They differ from residential care, where the person lives at the facility.
Megumi Morikawa: I’d like my mother to have daytime social contact, but I haven’t asked her yet.
Care worker: First, it matters to hear how your mother wants to spend her time. I cannot decide a particular service for her.
Megumi Morikawa: After speaking with her, I’d like to discuss conditions and costs. What should I do?
Care worker: I’ll check with the person responsible how to connect you with consultation. Check eligibility and costs there. No application has been made yet.
Megumi Morikawa: Understood. I’ll first hear my mother’s wishes, then check the consultation contact again.

kaigo-gap-services-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Separate consultation forms, personal choice and service applications
paragraphs: [Another practice situation] Megumi asks whether staff can start visiting her mother’s home tomorrow. Personal wishes, eligibility and start date are unconfirmed; no application was made. A simultaneous craft-material consultation accepts only item-name forms until October 17, with selection discussed with the person from the 18th. Materials themselves are not accepted.

Explain the home-visit form and unknowns to Megumi, distinguishing consultation-form receipt from selection and handover. Do not open personal records for general explanations or claim these three forms cover every service.

Example wording: A home visit means staff come to your home, but tomorrow’s availability, personal wishes and conditions are unconfirmed, and no application has been made. Until the 17th, we accept only consultation forms; from the 18th, we’ll discuss items with your mother. Please do not bring the materials themselves.

Next, tell Kawase-san that Megumi requested preparing the form with her mother. Personal consent is unconfirmed, consultation time undecided, and selection and handover not performed. Discuss a chance to hear the person and the consultation route. Do not report family requests as decisions by the absent person.

kaigo-gap-services-01-appointment-varian.heading: Check proposal, change request, availability and consent in order
paragraphs: [Staged learning practice] This arranges a craft-material consultation, not a medical appointment or service application. Until the 17th, only item-name forms are accepted; from the 18th, items are discussed with the person. No selection or handover occurred. Kawase proposed October 18 at 10:30 a.m., but Morikawa-san has not agreed. Home-visit wishes, conditions and start date are also unconfirmed.

At stage one, name the proposer and time and ask availability. At stage two, tell Kawase the person wants October 19 at 10:30 a.m. instead and wants to speak first without Megumi. Do not call the 19th confirmed at this point.

At stage three, communicate Kawase’s reply that October 19 at 10:30 a.m. can be reserved and ask consent again. At stage four, report the agreed time and attendee condition, preserving that item selection, handover and home-visit application remain undone.

Morikawa-san, Megumi-san asked to prepare a consultation form together. Kawase-san says a belongings discussion is possible on October 18 at 10:30 a.m. Would that suit you? We are not selecting or accepting items yet.
After Megumi-san’s request, Kawase-san proposed October 18 at 10:30 a.m. Does that suit you, Morikawa-san? Item selection and receipt are still to come.
The 18th doesn’t suit me. I could talk on the 19th at 10:30 a.m. Please speak with me first without calling Megumi.
